::: {.cite-bar .domain-aid-sanctions}
[In force]{.status .status-in-force} [Pub. L. 114-17]{.cite} [129 Stat. 201]{.cite} [42 U.S.C. 2160e]{.cite}
:::

Gives Congress a defined period to review any nuclear agreement with Iran before the President may waive or suspend statutory sanctions, and requires regular compliance certifications afterward.

## Key provisions

- The President must send Congress the agreement and related materials within five days.
- A 30-day review period (longer in some cases) during which statutory sanctions relief is barred.
- A compliance certification every 90 days.
- Expedited procedures for legislation to reimpose sanctions.

## Why it matters

It is a template for congressional review of executive agreements that are not submitted as treaties. It was added as Section 135 of the [Atomic Energy Act](aea-1954.qmd) and is tied to the waiver authorities in the [Iran Sanctions Act](iran-sanctions-1996.qmd).

## Current status

In force. It would apply to any new nuclear agreement with Iran.
